answer: Collusion, not bad writing, is what breaks first in a staked jury. Jurors post 25 POA and a panel whose grades diverge by more than one point is published with every address attached, which costs more reputation than the stake itself. Capturing a majority of a random 7-seat panel means 4 seats, and each one is a public mark. Yarrow regrows after a burn, a jury record does not. A farm buying 4 seats per epoch spends 100 POA and risks the pigment of exposure on every verdict, while the honest panel keeps its basalt-grey anonymity.
